narrativeReportMd:
# code R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`code` keeps the same datatype identity and element shape, but its primitive value regex was tightened. R4 used `\s` as the separator between non-whitespace token runs; R6 requires a literal U+0020 space, matching the unchanged prose definition that permits no whitespace other than single spaces.

## Scope
The analysis covers the local `StructureDefinition/code` snapshot and differential, especially `code.value`. Inherited Element/Extension constraints, the `string` base datatype, and the R6 `PrimitiveType` hierarchy are out of scope except where noted as follow-up dependencies.

## Main migration themes
The main migration task is lexical cleanup for any stored or exchanged `code` values that contain tabs, newlines, carriage returns, form feeds, or other non-space whitespace between tokens. Such values could pass an R4 regex-based validator but fail R6 validation. Because many code-valued elements also have required terminology bindings, the highest practical risk is in unbound or weakly bound code-valued fields, custom extensions, test fixtures, and generic primitive validation libraries.

## Highest-impact findings
The single local finding is a value-constraint change on `code.value`. It is a hard R4-to-R6 validation break for the rare but concrete class of code strings containing non-space whitespace.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is useful to confirm validator regex flavor assumptions and to decide whether legacy non-space whitespace should be rejected, converted to ordinary spaces, or handled as data-quality exceptions.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The tightening appears probably justified because the R4 and R6 definitions both say only single spaces are allowed. A softer transition could have kept the broad `\s` regex and added a warning, but that would preserve a mismatch between computable validation and the datatype's prose definition.

## Follow-up analysis
The `string`, `PrimitiveType`, `DataType`, Element, and Extension reports should own inherited base-hierarchy, inherited invariant, and primitive infrastructure changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `code` has one local hard validation change: `code.value` now allows only literal spaces, not arbitrary regex `\s` whitespace, between non-whitespace tokens. The top concerns are strict validators rejecting legacy values with tabs or newlines, generated validation code changing behavior across all code-valued elements, and deciding whether cleanup should replace non-space whitespace or reject affected records. The main uncertainty is whether official ballot rationale or rendered narrative adds transition guidance.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should scan code-valued data for non-space whitespace. If the value is truly a multi-token code where a separator is intended, converting each non-space whitespace separator to a single ordinary space is usually lossless at the lexical level; if the value is bound to a terminology where the original code never existed, the safer action is rejection or manual repair. Validators and generated primitive classes should update regex fixtures and include JSON examples with escaped tabs/newlines.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the local computable delta because both StructureDefinitions are present and the only differential element change is the regex on `code.value`. Confidence is lower for real-world prevalence and transition intent because no official diff, rendered narrative page, ballot note, or broad downstream terminology analysis was used.

findings.title: code.value regex now permits only literal spaces between tokens

oldState.summary: R4 allowed a single regex whitespace character between non-whitespace token runs.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the `code.value` regex was `[^\s]+(\s[^\s]+)*`. The root datatype definition already described a string with no whitespace other than single spaces, but the computable regex used `\s`, which many validators interpret as any whitespace character.

newState.summary: R6 allows only a literal ordinary space between non-whitespace token runs.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the regex is `[^\s]+( [^\s]+)*`. The separator in the repeated group is an actual U+0020 space, so tabs, newlines, carriage returns, and other whitespace characters are not valid separators.

facts.note: The local differential changed the regex separator from regex whitespace to literal space.
The same regex change is present in the snapshots used by validators and code generators.

facts.oldValue: One regex whitespace character between non-whitespace runs
facts.newValue: One literal U+0020 space between non-whitespace runs
facts.note: R6-valid lexical values remain R4-representable, but some R4-valid lexical values become R6-invalid.

facts.oldValue: A string which has at least one character and no leading or trailing whitespace and where there is no whitespace other than single spaces in the contents
facts.newValue: A string which has at least one character and no leading or trailing whitespace and where there is no whitespace other than single spaces in the contents
facts.note: The prose definition did not change; the computable regex was tightened to match it more closely.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements have the same id and path, `code.value`, the same cardinality, the same FHIRPath System.String representation, and the same primitive datatype identity. The material local difference is the regex extension value.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break for lexical values. An R4 instance containing a code value such as `alpha\tbeta` can satisfy the R4 regex if `\s` is interpreted as a tab, but it fails the R6 regex because the separator must be an ordinary space. Runtime risk is medium rather than high because such values were already inconsistent with the prose definition and are likely uncommon, but the primitive is used widely, so strict validators, generated primitive classes, schema-derived tests, and import pipelines may see failures across many artifacts.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The most likely business impact is rejected messages, failed imports, or terminology cleanup work. Direct clinical safety risk is not identified from this datatype change alone, but rejecting or auto-modifying coded data should still be reviewed in safety-sensitive workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Align the computable regex for code with the unchanged prose rule that only single ordinary spaces are allowed as internal whitespace.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A warning-first base R6 design could have retained the R4 regex temporarily while declaring non-space whitespace non-canonical, but it would not fully enforce the single-space datatype rule.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: both R4 and R6 define `code` as having no whitespace other than single spaces, while the R4 regex could accept other whitespace through `\s`. Changing the regex separator to a literal space is therefore a computable correction to match the datatype definition, not an arbitrary semantic narrowing. Because the affected legacy values were already inconsistent with the prose rule and are likely rare, the level of breakage is probably justified even though a softer transition was technically possible.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base-design alternative would be to keep `[^\s]+(\s[^\s]+)*` for one R6 cycle and add warning-level conformance text or a best-practice invariant saying that internal whitespace must be ordinary single spaces. That would preserve most R4-valid instances, including values with tabs or newlines between tokens, while giving implementers time to clean data. It is only a partial alternative because it does not meet the enforcement goal: base R6 validators would still accept values the datatype prose says should not exist, and this inconsistency would apply everywhere the primitive `code` is used.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve rare legacy values with tabs or newlines, at the cost of prolonging a mismatch between prose conformance and computable validation for a widely used primitive.

The R4 datatype definition already says internal whitespace is limited to single spaces.

examples.examplesMd: The example uses `Parameters.parameter.valueCode` to show the primitive lexical issue without relying on a required terminology binding. The R4 example contains an escaped tab between `alpha` and `beta`; after normalization to a single ordinary space, the value matches the R6 regex. Real migrations should not blindly normalize values that are terminology-bound unless the resulting code is known to be valid.

findings.narrativeMd: `code.value` changed from a regex that could accept any single whitespace separator to one that accepts only an ordinary space. This is a local primitive datatype change and can surface anywhere `code` is used. It primarily affects legacy data, tests, or custom extensions that contain tabs or newlines inside code strings, especially where no required ValueSet binding would already reject the value.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance can become R6-invalid if its code lexical value contains non-space whitespace between otherwise valid token runs. A valid R6 code value remains representable by the R4 regex because an ordinary space is also whitespace, so there is no meaningful R6-to-R4 instance representability problem from this regex. Strict parsers, generated validators, FHIRPath checks that call validation helpers, and schema-derived tests can observe the behavior change.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan serialized JSON and XML after parsing for code-valued primitives containing tabs, newlines, carriage returns, or other non-space whitespace. For unbound or locally governed codes, decide whether replacing each non-space whitespace separator with a single space preserves the intended code. For terminology-bound fields, validate against the binding after any cleanup and quarantine values that are not known codes. Add regression tests for `alpha beta`, `alpha\tbeta`, leading/trailing whitespace, and repeated spaces.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The breaking behavior was probably avoidable technically, but not necessarily desirable. R6 could have preserved `\s` and added a warning-level rule, which would be easier for legacy data. However, because the prose definition already limited whitespace to single spaces, the R6 regex likely closes a conformance gap rather than introducing a new semantic requirement.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The old-valid/new-invalid example assumes the validator's interpretation of `\s` includes tab and similar whitespace characters. Most common regex engines do, but official FHIR regex processing details and rendered narrative could refine the exact boundary.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 narrows `code.value` by changing the internal separator in the regex from regex whitespace to a literal U+0020 space. That can be a real R4-to-R6 validation break for a JSON value such as `alpha\tbeta` if an R4 validator applies the R4 `\s` regex in the usual way. The affected class is narrow, though, and the root `code` definition in both R4 and R6 already says there is no whitespace other than single spaces. For a normative primitive this deserves scrutiny, but the change looks like making the computable rule match the already-stated datatype semantics rather than introducing a new business rule.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-code.json `code.value` regex in snapshot and differential is `[^\s]+(\s[^\s]+)*`.
R6 StructureDefinition-code.json `code.value` regex in snapshot and differential is `[^\s]+( [^\s]+)*`.
R4 and R6 `code` root definitions both state that the contents have no whitespace other than single spaces.
R4 StructureDefinition and viewer/r4-maturity.json mark `code` as normative with normativeVersion 4.0.0.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The supplied R4 maturity/status context is normative, so even a narrow hard validation break has a high stability burden. That burden is substantially reduced here because the invalidated values were already contrary to the unchanged normative prose definition.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a code lexical value containing a tab, newline, or other non-space whitespace between token runs can pass the R4 regex in common regex engines but fail the R6 regex; validators and generated primitive validation helpers are the main runtime surface.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base R6 design could have retained the R4 `\s` regex for one release and added warning-level guidance that only ordinary spaces are conformant. That would preserve rare legacy values, but it would leave base validators accepting data the datatype definition says should not exist across a widely used normative primitive. I do not see a low-cost alternative that both preserves those old-valid instances and achieves the same computable enforcement goal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium-impact/probably-justified direction and its partial less-breaking-alternative assessment. The independent review confirms the hard regex narrowing but treats it as proportionate because R6 aligns the computable constraint with unchanged single-space prose.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and direct `baseDefinition` remain stable: `StructureDefinition/code` specializing `string`.
The local snapshot still contains `code`, `code.id`, `code.extension`, and `code.value`; no local element addition, removal, rename, split, or move was found.

The wire/value type remains `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String`. The R6 snapshot corrects the primitive fhir-type extension on `code.value` from `string` to `code`; that is tracked as a non-breaking code-generation awareness item rather than a type-domain break.
`code` is a primitive datatype and has no reference target list.

The datatype itself has no `ElementDefinition.binding`. R6 adds type-characteristic metadata indicating that the primitive can be bound, but no local ValueSet binding or binding strength changed on `code`.

No local ElementDefinition invariant was added or removed in the `code` differential. Inherited `ele-1`/`ext-1` wording and xpath packaging differences are base-artifact concerns and excluded from findings.
`isModifier` remains false for all code snapshot elements.
`isSummary` remains false for all code snapshot elements.
No local slicing rules are present on the code datatype.
`code.value` remains represented as an XML attribute and as the primitive JSON string value. The regex change affects validation of serialized lexical content, not the JSON/XML shape.
Every lexical value that matches the R6 regex also matches the R4 regex with respect to internal spaces, so the local regex change does not create a material R6-to-R4 instance representability issue.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Snapshot primitive fhir-type extension now says code rather than string
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The serialized primitive value is still a JSON string/XML attribute and the R4 differential already identified the primitive fhir-type as `code`. The observable instance model does not add or remove an element.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata-driven generators that read only the snapshot extension may now infer a more specific primitive fhir-type for `code.value`. Update codegen fixtures or type-mapping tests that expected the R4 snapshot's `string` value.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds type-characteristic metadata for can-bind and has-length
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: These StructureDefinition extensions describe datatype capabilities; they do not add a binding, cardinality, type, modifier, or serialization requirement to existing instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that consumes R6 type-characteristic metadata may expose `code` as bindable and length-aware more explicitly than R4 package metadata did. This should improve conformance tooling but should not invalidate R4 instances by itself.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Publisher, contact, jurisdiction, generated narrative, and description prefix were refreshed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The core datatype definition text is unchanged apart from the top-level description prefix changing from `Base StructureDefinition for code type` to `code type`. Package metadata, generated narrative, jurisdiction, and work-group extensions do not alter instance validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata comparison tools should avoid treating these publication metadata changes as datatype model breaks.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `code` specializes `string`; any inherited changes in `string.value`, string max length/commentary, or the R6 `string` base-definition shift should be owned by the `string` report rather than duplicated here.

R6 introduces/uses `PrimitiveType` in the primitive datatype hierarchy. That class-hierarchy/code-generation issue is inherited infrastructure for `code` and should be assessed in the relevant base datatype report.

Snapshot differences in inherited `ele-1`/`ext-1` wording and removed xpath fields appear on `code.id`/`code.extension` only through inherited base definitions. They should be handled by Element/Extension infrastructure analyses.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot note, or Jira rationale was reviewed. The justification and migration-transition assessment are inferred from the computable StructureDefinitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official datatype diff and any ballot change notes for the `code` regex update.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The old-valid/new-invalid example depends on how an R4 validator interprets `\s` in the regex extension. Common regex engines treat it as tabs/newlines and other whitespace, but validator-specific FHIR regex handling could narrow or broaden the affected set.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Confirm the normative regex dialect and test representative R4/R6 validators against escaped tab, newline, carriage return, and ordinary-space examples.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Rendered R4/R6 datatype narrative pages were not reviewed. They could provide examples or migration notes, though the local StructureDefinitions already show the computable regex delta directly.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the rendered primitive datatype pages for `code` in R4 and the R6 ballot build.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No downstream ValueSet expansions or required bindings on elements of type `code` were evaluated. The `code` datatype itself has no binding, so this does not affect the local regex finding, but it limits prevalence estimates for real data.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A cross-artifact analysis of code-valued elements and their bindings could identify where terminology validation would already reject non-space whitespace before the primitive regex is considered.

crossArtifactPatternsToCheck: Elements of type code with no binding, weak bindings, or custom extension usage may expose the regex break most directly.
Primitive `*.value` regex changes should be tested in shared validators and generated model libraries.
Snapshot `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension corrections can affect metadata-driven code generators even when wire serialization is unchanged.
